text:
lina: Quick question — I just got a jury summons for Tue May 12. That's smack in the middle of our sprint blackout. Can I swap one of my floating holidays to cover that day, or do I need to use PTO? Also if I can't swap because of the blackout, what happens to the unused floating day?
people-ops: Hi @lina — thanks for flagging. Short answers: jury duty is a protected event, so we don't require you to burn PTO if you provide the summons PDF. We can also process a floating-holiday swap as an exception to the blackout. Please submit the jury doc + the swap request form and we'll mark it a blackout exception. :white_check_mark:
people-ops: Steps: 1) Upload summons to the HR portal. 2) Fill the Leave Swap form (link below) and select "Jury duty — blackout exception". 3) CC your manager for approval. HR will finalize and notify payroll. Link: https://hr.internal/redwood/forms/leave-swap
lina: Awesome — thanks. If I prefer the swap (so my floating day gets used instead of being recorded as jury), does that change pay?
payroll-bot: @lina FYI: Jury pay rules — jury time is paid per local law. If you choose to have the day recorded as a floating holiday instead, payroll will process it as a regular paid day (no jury stipend). Either way you won't be charged PTO. If you'd like the payroll team to choose the option that preserves more PTO for you, add a note in the form.
samir: I can approve on my side. @people-ops — once she files, I’ll ping you. Lina — send me the summons when you upload so I can sign off quickly. :+1:
people-ops: Thanks @samir — we'll need manager ack in the form. One important policy note for cleanup: floating holidays generally do not auto-carry into the next calendar year unless approved by people ops during the year-end rollover. Exceptions are rare and require exec sign-off. If you can't swap now and end up with an unused floating day, it will either expire per the annual policy or be handled under the one-off exception process (not an automatic payout).
jenna: Adding operational detail from benefits side — contractors vs full-time rule: contractors do not get floating holiday payouts; full-time employees may be eligible for a cash-out in limited circumstances during offboarding or with approval. If you're FTE you can ask for an exception but it's not guaranteed.
lina: Got it. I'll upload the summons and fill the form now. Thanks everyone.
people-ops: Perfect — we’ll process this as a blackout exception for jury duty once the docs are in. ETA ~1 business day to update your record and notify payroll. If you need an immediate confirmation for your manager today, reply here and @jenna will post the temporary note.
lina: Quick follow-up — if jury duty runs multiple days, do I need a separate form for each day?
people-ops: If consecutive days, one form with start/end dates + attaching the summons is fine. If non-consecutive, submit a single request listing all dates. Also include any court paperwork that shows multi-day service.
hr-bot: Automatic reminder — leave-swap form submitted without attachment will be marked incomplete. Attachments accepted: PDF, JPG. If you need help scanning, reply and we can help.
people-ops: Closing note: blackout exceptions are limited to protected leaves (jury, bereavement in some regions, medical). Vacation swaps for non-protected events still require normal blackout approval flow and are subject to operational needs.
lina: Thanks again — filing now.
